title: Backend developer (.NET)
summary: From your first line of C# to a containerised, database-backed ASP.NET Core API with CI, auth and the performance habits a production service needs.
outcome: Ready to pick up backend tickets on a .NET team: build the endpoint, write the migration, secure it, containerise it and ship it through CI.

stages.title: C# you can read and write
stages.why: Every backend ticket is C# first. Types, control flow, collections and exceptions are what code review checks before anything else, so they come before frameworks.
stages.milestone: Writes small, tested console tools in idiomatic C# and reads a stack trace to its cause

stages.title: The tools you use every day
stages.why: On day one you clone a repo, branch, rebase and open a pull request. Git and a shell are the difference between being productive in week one and waiting for help.
stages.milestone: Works on a team repository: branches, rebases, resolves conflicts and opens a clean pull request

stages.title: Modern C#: LINQ, async and your first API
stages.why: Services spend their life waiting on I/O and shaping data. async/await and LINQ are how .NET does both, and the Tasks API project puts them behind real HTTP endpoints with dependency injection and middleware.
stages.milestone: Builds a small ASP.NET Core API with async I/O, dependency injection and middleware

stages.title: Data that survives a restart
stages.why: Nearly every backend owns a database. SQL first, so you know what EF Core generates, then EF Core itself: modelling, relationships, change tracking and migrations you can run in production.
stages.milestone: Ships a database-backed API with migrations and queries that do not N+1

stages.title: Code a reviewer approves
stages.why: Working code is the start of a review, not the end. Readable names, SOLID where it pays, testable seams and safe refactoring are what senior engineers comment on.
stages.milestone: Refactors a tangled class behind tests and explains the trade-offs in review

stages.title: HTTP and security
stages.why: An API is an HTTP contract and an attack surface. Status codes, caching and headers, then JWTs and ASP.NET Core authentication, ending with an API you secure yourself.
stages.milestone: Secures an API with JWT bearer auth and policies, and can explain each 401 and 403

stages.title: Ship it: containers and CI
stages.why: Code that only runs on your laptop is not done. A multi-stage Dockerfile, Compose with a real database and a pipeline that tests every pull request are how teams deliver.
stages.milestone: Can ship a containerised API with CI

stages.title: Production-grade services
stages.why: Real traffic brings retries, duplicates, slow queries and memory pressure. Messaging guarantees, query performance and advanced C# make the difference when something breaks at 2 a.m.
stages.milestone: Owns a production service: idempotent consumers, fast queries and a capstone shipped end to end
